newsitem.title: DUBAI: At least 30 dead after haj blaze in Saudi-diplomat.
newsitem.headline: At least 30 dead after haj blaze in Saudi-diplomat.

text.p: At least 30 haj pilgrims, all believed to be Pakistanis, died on Tuesday in a blaze at a tent compound near the Islamic holy city of Mecca, Pakistan's ambassador to Saudi Arabia said.

"Thirty are believed to be dead. We fear they may all be Pakistanis," Ambassador Shahed Amin, who visited the site of the fire in Mena, told Reuters from Mecca by telephone. "There are probably more (dead) but I cannot speak for other nationalities."
The official Saudi Press Agency said the fire started at 11.45 a.m. (0845 GMT) at a bridge linking Mecca and Mena and spread to Mena -- the site of the tent compound -- due to heavy winds.
Amin said: "The fire is under control and the situation is calm and orderly now."
The ambassador said about 30,000 people were in the Pakistani camp. "There has been extensive damage to about 50,000 tents" across the tent city, he said, adding he did not know how the fire started.
He said 50 out of 3,000 Pakistani tents were badly damaged and arrangements were being made to house the displaced people.
